3. The respondent No. 7 contested the Rule submitted affidavit-in-opposition denying the material statement contending, inter-alia, that the land measuring 1.11 acres in plot No. 65 appertaining to C. S. Khatian No. 6947 of mouza Shahar Dhaka under Police Station Kotwali belonged to Karuna Das Bahadur transferred 8 bighas of land including C. S. Plot No. 65 to one Sheikh Shefatullah. Sheikh Shefatullah transferred the same in Elahi Box Driver by dint of registered sale deed on 3rd Magh, 1326 13. S. Elahi Box Driver owned and possessed that land and subsequently on 04.07.1928 transferred 3(three) pakhis of land with specific boundary of Bhuban Mohan Ghose vide registered deed No. 2615. Bhuban Mohan Ghose as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 1537 of 1929 against Elahi Box and others in the 3rd Court of Munsif, Dhaka 'for declaration of title and recovery of 'Kha' possession far it relates to C. S. Plot No. 94. In that suit Elahi Box filed written statement contesting the suit land eventually the suit was dismissed by the trial Court on 23.03.1931 but the findings of possession was in favour of the plaintiff as regards to C. S. Plot No. 65. 

 4. Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, learned Counsel, appearing for the petitioners submitted that the C.S. Plot No. 65 is the debuttor property and the said property by Karuna Das Bose by a registered arpannama dated 01.05.1914 in favour of Sree Sree Laxmi Narayan Jew Tagore and the C.S. Khatian No. 6947 was rightly prepared in the name of the said Sree Sree Laxmi Narayan Jew Tagore being represented by Shebayet Karuna Das Bose Bahadur and the writ-respondent No.7's predecessors are the monthly tenants under Shebayet of the said debtor property and the scheme of the proper management of the debuttor property was declared by judgment and decree passed by Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 56 of 1944 and since then the said debuttor property is being run by the Shebayets and the said debuttor property has never by transferred; that the C. S. Plot No. 65 is the debuttor property and the respondent Rajuk has illegally approved the plan in favour of the writ-respondent No. 7 for construction of 20 storied building in C. S.. Plot No. 65 which is debuttor property and writ-respondent No. 7 obtained some certificates from various departments only mentioning 37/2 Purana Paum and with respect to C.S. Plot No. 65 but writ-respondent: No. 7 obtained plan from RAJUK to construct 16 storied building in C.S. Plot No. 94 and 95(part) and 65 by suppression of facts and when he started construction in C. S. Plot No. 65 then it was brought to the knowledge of RAJUK and RAJUK issued a notice upon the writ-respondent No. 7 to show cause as to whey the approved plan should not be cancelled and stopped the construction work and the writ-respondent No. 7 challenging the said notice filed writ petition No. 6875 of 20078 and in the said writ petition the High Court Division found that the C. S. Plot No. 65 is the debuttor property and finally discharged the Rule but thereafter, RAJUK illegally allowed writ-respondent No. 7 to make construction on C. S. Plot No. 65 which is a debuttor property. The learned Counsel further submitted that the predecessors of writ-respondent - No. 7 and also respondent No. 7 were the monthly ten-ants under Shebayet of the said debtor property and respondent No.7 and his brothers in collusion with the dishonest employees of settlement department got S.A. record in their name but in respect of C.S. Plot No. 65 they have no deed by which they ban claim the title of the said plot and in the absence of deed in respect of C. S. Plot No. 65 RA.JUK can not allow respondent No. 7 to make construction on the said plot; that the subject matter of the writ petition and Title Suit No. 1633 of 2008 are not the same or similar as because Title Suit No. 1633 of 2008 filed by the petitioner as plaintiff for of title and recovery of khas possession and the writ petition was filed challenging the action of RAJUK whereby RAJUK approved the plan in favour of respondent No. 7 and his 'brother to construct 16 storied corn-metrical-cum-residential building in C. S. Plot No. 65 which is debuttor property. The learned Counsel also submitted that there is not on record to show that the beet land is the land of. Annexure- A or Anncxure-K unless a relayment is made and report is obtained showing the land of C. S. Plot No.65 is identical with land of schedule 3 of the Annexure-A and Annexure-K it is difficult on the part of the Court sitting in writ jurisdiction to hold that the land of Plot No. 65 of mouza Shahar .Dhaka attracts the lands of schedule 'C' of Annexure-A. It appears that according to C. S. Plot No. 65 is a debuttor property to which writ-respondent No. 7 did not claim as title by any title deed and hence further enquiry as opined by the High Court Division is unnecessary for the purpose of considering the legality of the actions of RAJUK and therefore, the judgment of the High Court Division is not sustainable in law. 

 5. It appears that there is no mention of plot number either in Annxure-A or in Annexurc-K. There is no other document available on record to show that the property as described in schedule of the Annexure-A and Annexure-K to the writ petition and supplementary affidavit filed by the petitioner are identical with the land of C.S. Plot No. 65 mouza Shahar Dhaka. It further appears that the plot No. 65 has been recorded as 'beel'. There is nothing on record to show that the said been land is the land of Annexurc-A or Annexurc-K. Unless a relayment is made and a report is obtained showing the land of C.S. Plot No. 65 is identical with the land of schedule-3 of the Annexure-A and schedule-5 of the Annexure-K it is difficult on the part of this Court, sitting in writ jurisdiction to hold that the land of plot No. 65 of inouza Shahar Dhaka attracts the lands of schedule-C of Annexure-A and Annexure-K. Whether or not the said plot No. 65 is identical with Annexure-K and Annexure-A is a question of fact and it could be resolved in a regular title suit by making repayment by an Advocate Commissioner and other support evidence on record and the same could not be the subject matter of writ petition. Admittedly the petitioners being out of possession has instituted the suit for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession. It appears that S.A. record, R.S. record and mutated Khatian stood prepared in the name of the represented No. 7 and others and their predecessors. Admittedly the respondents are in possession by paying rent and taxes since 1965, it is difficult to hold that the approval made by the respondent Nos. 3 and 5 were without having any law authority.
